subs: Beds on its Medicare cost report. A licensed bed count usually runs higher.
Each inpatient stay that ended counts once, whoever paid for it.
All inpatient days divided by discharges. Answer in days, like 4.5.
Patient days divided by the bed days it had available.
Medicare Advantage plans included. Counted in days spent in a bed, not in people.
Medicaid managed care plans included. Counted in days spent in a bed, not in people.
Two half-time employees count as one. Hospital payroll only: not clinics, not contract staff.
From AHRQ's 2023 list of who owns which hospital, matched to Medicare's hospital list.
Out of every hospital in Alaska on Medicare's list, every kind counted.
Small rural hospitals with 25 inpatient beds at most, paid by Medicare on their costs.
Every one of its hospitals' latest Medicare cost report, added up.
Biggest by beds on its cost report. The answer names the hospital.
Two half-time employees count as one. Hospital payrolls only: clinics, offices and any health plan are left out.

questions.q: How many full-time-equivalent employees did Petersburg Medical Center have on its payroll in fiscal 2025?
questions.why: About 11.8 for every bed.

questions.q: How many full-time-equivalent employees did Searhc Wrangell Medical Center & LTC have on its payroll in fiscal 2024?
questions.why: About 22.4 for every bed.

questions.q: How many full-time-equivalent employees do Southeast Alaska Regional Health Consortium's hospitals have on payroll, added together?
questions.why: From all 3 hospitals' latest cost reports, mostly 2024.

questions.q: What percent of Petersburg Medical Center's inpatient days in fiscal 2025 were for Medicare patients?
questions.why: Traditional Medicare was 60 percent and Medicare Advantage plans 0 percent.

questions.q: What percent of Southeast Alaska Regional Health Consortium's inpatient days in fiscal 2024 were for Medicare patients?
questions.why: Traditional Medicare was 49 percent and Medicare Advantage plans 0 percent.

questions.q: What percent of Petersburg Medical Center's inpatient days in fiscal 2025 were for Medicaid patients?
questions.why: Traditional Medicaid was 26 percent and Medicaid managed care plans 0 percent.

questions.q: What percent of Southeast Alaska Regional Health Consortium's inpatient days in fiscal 2024 were for Medicaid patients?
questions.why: Traditional Medicaid was 21 percent and Medicaid managed care plans 0 percent.

questions.q: How many beds did Petersburg Medical Center report to Medicare for fiscal 2025?
questions.why: That ranks second of 3 Southeast Alaska Regional Health Consortium hospitals; Southeast Alaska Regional Health Consortium has the most, 25 beds.

questions.q: How many beds did Searhc Wrangell Medical Center & LTC report to Medicare for fiscal 2024?
questions.why: That is the fewest of 3 Southeast Alaska Regional Health Consortium hospitals; Southeast Alaska Regional Health Consortium has the most, 25 beds.

questions.q: How many beds did Southeast Alaska Regional Health Consortium report to Medicare for fiscal 2024?
questions.why: No other Southeast Alaska Regional Health Consortium hospital reports more; Petersburg Medical Center is next at 12 beds.

questions.q: How many inpatient discharges did Petersburg Medical Center report for fiscal 2025?
questions.why: About 0 a day.

questions.q: How many inpatient discharges did Southeast Alaska Regional Health Consortium report for fiscal 2024?
questions.why: About 2 a day.

questions.q: How many days did the average inpatient stay last at Southeast Alaska Regional Health Consortium in fiscal 2024?
questions.why: Across the cost reports of U.S. general hospitals it averages 5.0 days.

questions.q: On an average day in fiscal 2025, what percent of Petersburg Medical Center's beds had a patient in them?
questions.why: No other Southeast Alaska Regional Health Consortium hospital ran fuller; Southeast Alaska Regional Health Consortium is next at 34 percent.

questions.q: On an average day in fiscal 2024, what percent of Searhc Wrangell Medical Center & LTC's beds had a patient in them?
questions.why: That is the emptiest of 3 Southeast Alaska Regional Health Consortium hospitals; Petersburg Medical Center ran fullest, 39 percent.

questions.q: On an average day in fiscal 2024, what percent of Southeast Alaska Regional Health Consortium's beds had a patient in them?
questions.why: That ranks second of 3 Southeast Alaska Regional Health Consortium hospitals; Petersburg Medical Center ran fullest, 39 percent.

questions.q: How many hospitals does Southeast Alaska Regional Health Consortium run, by the federal list of health systems?
questions.why: All of them are in Alaska. A system's own count can differ: it may count campuses on their own, or hospitals that joined after 2023.

questions.q: What percent of the hospitals in Alaska belong to Southeast Alaska Regional Health Consortium?
questions.why: 3 of 25. The next biggest system there, Providence, has 4.

questions.q: How many of Southeast Alaska Regional Health Consortium's hospitals are critical access hospitals?
questions.why: They are Petersburg Medical Center, Searhc Wrangell Medical Center & LTC and Southeast Alaska Regional Health Consortium.

questions.q: How many beds do Southeast Alaska Regional Health Consortium's hospitals report to Medicare, added together?
questions.why: From all 3 hospitals' latest cost reports, mostly 2024.

questions.q: How many beds does Southeast Alaska Regional Health Consortium's biggest hospital report to Medicare?
questions.why: It is Southeast Alaska Regional Health Consortium. Petersburg Medical Center is next, with 12.
